Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_citations¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_citations(const Note& other) const

Shared Citation Markers Between Two Notes¶

intersect_citations(other) reduces each cell to its set of citation markers and returns the markers present in both cells as a TokenBatch. It is the citation-set member of the set-similarity family; the scoring members are jaccard_citations and overlap_citations.

How the set is built¶

A citation marker is either

  • a bracketed number — [ then one to three digits then ] ([1], [42], [100]), or

  • an author–year group — ( then a capitalized name then , then a four-digit year (optionally with a letter suffix) then ) — for example (Smith, 2020) or (Lee, 2021a).

Markers are kept with their brackets and lowercased for comparison. A cell with no [ or ( and no digit produces an empty set. The set is deduplicated.

What is emitted¶

Members in both sets, in the order they first appear in self, once each; a cell with no shared marker contributes an empty range. The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_citations requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_citations expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Shared Numbered References¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"see [1] and [2] and [10]"})
                       .nlp().intersect_citations(pluss::make_note({"refer to [2], [3], [10]"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["[2]", "[10]"]
offsets: [0, 2]

[2] and [10] appear in both cells; [1] and [3] do not. The brackets are part of each token.
